sentences.text:
Smt. Prasanthi vs R.Laxmanna on 25 September, 2025
 The Hon'Ble Justice Moushumi Bhattacharya
 And
 The Hon'Ble Justice Gadi Praveen Kumar
 CMA.No.1007 of 2010
Judgment:

(Per Hon'ble Justice Moushumi Bhattacharya) The Civil Miscellaneous Appeal arises out of an order dated 30.07.2010 passed by the Senior Civil Judge, Gadwal ('Trial Court') in HMOP.No.26 of 2008 filed by the respondent/husband under sections 13(1)(ia) and (ib) of The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking dissolution of his marriage with the appellant/wife on the grounds of cruelty and desertion.
2. The Trial Court allowed the petition filed by the respondent while observing that the respondent had established both cruelty and desertion by way of oral and documentary evidence.
The Trial Court accordingly proceeded to grant a decree of divorce thereby dissolving the marriage between the appellant and the respondent solemnized on 24.06.1999.
3. Aggrieved by the impugned Order allowing the petition of the respondent/husband, the appellant/wife has preferred the present Appeal.
The Appeal has been pending before this Court since 2010.
4. On 08.12.2010, a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court granted interim suspension of the impugned order and issued notice to the respondent.
However, the respondent/husband remained unrepresented despite service of notice and filing of vakalat.
None of the Proceeding Sheets from 08.12.2010 to 28.08.2025 record any representation on behalf of the respondent/husband.
On 06.08.2025, another Co-ordinate Bench directed the Appeal to be listed under the caption 'For Dismissal' on the ground of the appellant/wife not being represented.
When the Appeal came before us on 21.08.2025, learned counsel appearing for the appellant/wife submitted that he needed to take necessary instructions from the appellant/wife.
The matter was thereafter taken up on two occasions.
On the last occasion i.e., on 28.08.2025, counsel submitted that he had not received any instructions from the appellant/wife with regard to the Appeal.
We hence reserved the Appeal for judgment on that date.

5. The impugned Order framed the issue, namely, whether the respondent/husband (the petitioner before the Trial Court) is entitled to divorce under the grounds of cruelty and desertion under the provisions of the 1955 Act.
6. The factual findings of the Trial Court are as follows:
( i) The marriage between the parties was solemnized on 24.06.1999 and the parties had two children thereafter.

(iii) A Maintenance Case vide M.C.No.4 of 2006 before the Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Gadwal was decided in favour of the appellant/wife by ordering the respondent/husband to pay Rs.2000/- per month to the appellant.

sentences.text: (iv) PW.1 (the respondent/husband herein) deposed that the parties lived happily for two years after marriage.
Thereafter, the attitude of the appellant/wife changed which led to frequent petty quarrel's between the parties.
(v) In the month of July, 2000, the appellant left the society of the respondent/husband and went to live with her mother.
(vi) The respondent/husband went to the house of the appellant's mother several times to bring the appellant/wife back to the matrimonial home.
However, the appellant hardly lived for one month at her matrimonial home before returning to her mother's house without the respondent's consent.

(vii) The 'tendency' (in the words of the Trial Court') of the appellant of returning to her mother's house 9 - 10 times and then finally leaving the respondent's Society on 05.11.2002 shows that the appellant deserted the respondent.
(viii) The appellant/wife acted as per the whims and fancies of her mother and neglected and deserted the respondent.
(ix) The appellant/wife treated the respondent/husband with such cruelty so much so that it would be harmful and injurious to the respondent/husband to live with the appellant/wife.

(x) The respondent deposed in his evidence that the appellant/wife filed a false criminal case against the respondent/husband vide C.C.No.3 of 2006 under sections 498-A and 506 of the IPC before the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Alampur.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Alampur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant thereafter got the Criminal Case compounded through a compromise before the Lok Adalat, Alampur on 31.12.2007 by taking Rs.1,20,000/- towards permanent alimony.
(xi) The appellant/wife is an obstinate person and there is no chance of reunion between the parties.

(xii) The appellant/wife was examined as RW.1 wherein she stated that the respondent had started harassing her by demanding an additional dowry of Rs.1 lakh and the respondent had filed an earlier divorce petition in 2003 vide O.P.No.27 of 2003 which was compromised on the advice of elders.

(xiii) The appellant/wife admitted to filing a Criminal Case under sections 498-A and 506 of the IPC before the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Alampur vide C.C.No.03 of 2006 which was compromised before the Lok Adalat Bench at Alampur on 31.12.2007 through the payment of Rs.1,20,000/- towards permanent alimony by the respondent as well as a Maintenance case vide M.C.No.4 of 2006 before the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Gadwal whereby the respondent was ordered to pay Rs.2,000/- per month to the appellant/wife.

sentences.text: (xiv) The evidence of RW.2 (mother of the appellant) corroborated the evidence given by the appellant/wife that the appellant left the company of the respondent/husband without the consent of the respondent/husband.
(xv) The appellant/wife has been living with her mother for the last six years.
(xvi) The Cross-examination of the parties revealed that there were 'petty quarrels' between the parties.
(xvii) The marriage between the parties had irretrievably broken down.
7. The above findings led the Trial Court to hold that the appellant had deserted the respondent of her free will, without any sufficient reasons.

The Trial Court held that the respondent is entitled for divorce on the ground of desertion since the appellant's mother had categorically admitted that the appellant had been residing with her since the last six years without any reasonable cause.
8. We have carefully perused the impugned order dated 30.07.2010, allowing the divorce petition filed by the respondent/husband on the grounds of desertion and cruelty.

We find that the reasons given by the appellant for leaving the company of the respondent and staying with her mother for six to eight years prior to filing of the divorce petition has not been recorded or considered in the impugned order, inspite of the appellant having categorically deposed that she was forced to leave the company of the respondent by reason of demand for additional dowry and the respondent's adulterous relationship with a third person.
The Trial Court has not dealt with this issue or recorded the evidence given by the appellant in detail.
9. The impugned order is replete into conclusions which are not supported either by the pleadings or the evidence adduced by the parties.

The Trial Court's view with regard to the appellant having an obligation to live in the place of the respondent's employment and arriving at the conclusion that the appellant behaved arbitrarily without any reason, is reflective of this pre-conceived mindset.
The finding that the marriage between the parties had irretrievably broken down is also without any reasons or evidence.
10. We are of the firm view that mere filing of a Criminal Case under section 498A of the IPC will not amount to cruelty so as to entitle the respondent to file a petition for divorce.
Even otherwise, the impugned order lacks clarity in terms of segregation of facts, findings and conclusions.
We accordingly accept the interim suspension granted by a Co-ordinate Bench on 08.12.2010 which has been continued till date.

3 11.
As stated above, the respondent has remained unrepresented in the Appeal.
It is clear that neither of the parties are interested to pursue the Appeal.
We however do not find any reason to dismiss the Appeal by confirming the impugned order in view of the infirmities therein as stated above.
12. CMA.No.1007 of 2010, along with all connected applications, is accordingly allowed.
The impugned Order dated 30.07.2010 is set aside.
Consequentially, the decree dated 30.07.2010 granting divorce is also set aside.
